originality.rationale: A published more general weighted odd-cycle fourth-power theorem gives n²(16-Λ_{n,a})→6μ(a) on odd cycles; for constant weight a=1 its μ=π². Under sign alternation, an odd-cycle difference operator is exactly the submitted antiperiodic I+U_n (for odd n), and fourth-power-to-operator-norm conversion yields 3π²/16 identically. More decisively, the full published proof works directly on antiperiodic nodal arrays and after the gauge conversion never uses odd parity; its exact quartic defect e=16E, transformed g, local coefficient 6=16*(3/8), H¹ lower bound and recovery apply unchanged to the even signed-shift dimensions. Thus the all-n claim is covered by a routine parity-free reading of the stronger weighted theorem; merely restating in signed 2n-cycle language does not add independent novelty. A second same-shift published numerical-radius theorem treats a different operator invariant and was explicitly distinguished.
residual_risks: No historical claim about which same-day findings came first; mathematically the public weighted result’s proof covers the submitted problem.
The prior weighted theorem states odd n, but its proof does not use parity after antiperiodic reduction; the even signed-shift extension is routine rather than a new structural contribution.
